opencode.note: OpenCode v2 never auto-updates under OLYMPUS. The vendored CLI is updated only after the isolated conformance gate approves the exact version; an untested update can break sessions, the v2 API, MCP or the DB schema.

releases.title: Hibernation v2, GO truth and the smart burn
highlights: X now quits by default; hibernate is explicit (tray, lock, or the close-to-hibernate preference). A real quit stops the preview/MCP fleet instead of leaving it in the app cgroup.
Hibernate waits for a streaming chat turn, keeps a preview only when a live hop needs it, records the servers it stops, and the wake restores them automatically.
The hibernation HUD has a collapse button: 420×720 → 340×190 (campaign, GO month, in-flight hop only); expand restores the full widget.
The GO graph uses the console anchor (monthly/5h/weekly) plus the local delta; the weekly window resets Monday 00:00 UTC. The measured 25.1% / 50.1% matches the console's 25% / on-pace-50%.

Smart burn chooses a GO-only roster at the next hop/message (Kimi K3, Kimi K2.7 Code, DeepSeek 1017, Qwen3.7 Plus, MiniMax M3). Claude Opus/Sonnet are Zen models, not in the GO catalog; the screen says so instead of guessing.
The burn toggle never rewrites opencode.json and never cuts a live turn; it applies at the hop/message boundary and diversifies top lanes so one per-model cap cannot carry all ten gods.
OpenCode v2 2.3.2 remains the latest npm release and is gate-approved; the patch-notes screen checks the live latest on every open.
A tag-icon/logo audit and a 24px vector brief are in docs/design/TAG-ICON-BRIEF.md; the 16px marks are hand-authored, not model-generated.
Wake ignores ERR_ABORTED (the splash → APP_URL navigation) instead of entering a reload loop; the preview restore probes and retries until verified.
Max Quality / strategy apply resolves the real app root in standalone (not .next/standalone); the L4 probe falls back to the package binary. Verified ok:true.

releases.title: OpenCode 2.3.2 alignment and the patch-notes screen
highlights: OpenCode v2 2.3.2 passed the isolated conformance gate (serve, v2 sessions, prompt/SSE, DB schema, tokens, abort) and a real Apollo turn.
The boot loader now shows a What's new card after the first second; a hibernate return repaints the same loader, so the alignment is visible during a slow wake.
A status-bar Patch notes button opens the full updates screen from anywhere; /patch-notes is also a standalone page.
The screen reads the installed and npm-latest OpenCode versions live and takes the tested version from patch-notes.json, so it stays updatable without hardcoding the UI.
The update lane still refuses an ungated version and shows the conformance command instead of updating blind.

releases.title: The preview that obeys, the marks that cannot be lost
highlights: Browser previews keep 127.0.0.1 (the project session survives); Electron alone uses the isolated 127.0.0.2 OOPIF origin for 60 FPS.
Apollo mark batches are durable background plans with plan/latest/retry, a 20-minute budget and boot-aware stale recovery.
The small preview sends to Apollo; every non-quick mark is saved to the project queue before the turn.
Hibernation stops managed dev servers and prunes an expired window; dev servers report RSS, adopt the true port owner and restart in place.
Next.js 16.4.6 closes the advisory that made 16.4.2 fail the build.

releases.title: Performance: the preview gets its own renderer
highlights: Electron runs the live preview as an OOPIF on 127.0.0.2; AIME measured parent 54 → 60 FPS and iframe 52 → 60 FPS.
GPU is on by default; a persisted software-rendering marker was retired.
Progressive boot waits for the shell, not nine panel endpoints; heavy panes show their own branded loaders.
